response.sql: SELECT e.status AS status, AVG(b.amount - b.spent) AS avg_amount_minus_spent, COUNT(*) AS line_count FROM budget b JOIN event e ON e.event_id = b.link_to_event WHERE b.spent >= 6.0 GROUP BY e.status;

assumptions.assumption: The join is an inner join on exact text equality of event.event_id and budget.link_to_event, so budget lines with no matching event are dropped.
The spent >= 6.0 filter is applied to each budget line before grouping, and lines with NULL spent are excluded by that filter.
AVG ignores rows where amount - spent is NULL (for example, a NULL amount), and AVG returns NULL (blank) for a status with no such rows.
line_count counts all qualifying budget lines (COUNT(*)), including any with a NULL amount, since the request says 'the number of such budget lines'.
status means event.status, as written in the request, and it is grouped directly; a NULL event status forms its own group.

alternatives.interpretation: Count only the budget lines that contribute to the average, i.e. those where amount - spent is not missing.
alternatives.sql: SELECT e.status AS status, AVG(b.amount - b.spent) AS avg_amount_minus_spent, COUNT(b.amount - b.spent) AS line_count FROM budget b JOIN event e ON e.event_id = b.link_to_event WHERE b.spent >= 6.0 GROUP BY e.status;
